title: Bill Ackman Returns to Netflix With Six New Stock Bets
excerpt: Pershing Square disclosed new positions in Netflix, Visa, Mastercard, and three other companies in a second-quarter letter, deploying nearly $5 billion from its new closed-end fund.
body:
• Bill Ackman's Pershing Square has taken a new stake in Netflix, returning to the streaming giant after a $400 million loss in 2022
  • The hedge fund also initiated positions in Visa, Mastercard, S&P Global, Intercontinental Exchange, and Alcon in the first half of 2026
  • Pershing Square has deployed nearly $5 billion in its new closed-end fund since its IPO earlier this year
  • Ackman argues Netflix has "effectively won the streaming wars" with a subscriber base that exceeds any competitor by a wide margin

Billionaire investor Bill Ackman has returned to Netflix, taking a new stake in the streaming giant just a few years after exiting the stock at a roughly $400 million loss — a move he described at the time as driven by a "loss of confidence" in the company's future.

In a second-quarter letter to investors released Wednesday, Ackman and Pershing Square chief investment officer Ryan Israel disclosed that the hedge fund built positions in six new stocks during the first half of 2026, including Netflix, Visa, Mastercard, S&P Global, Intercontinental Exchange, and Alcon.

A Second Chance on Streaming

Ackman first bought Netflix shares in early 2022, only to dump them months later after a subscriber growth slowdown shattered confidence. The experience cost Pershing Square approximately $400 million.

"Netflix has since effectively won the streaming wars. Its subscriber base now exceeds any competitor's by a wide margin, and that scale is self-reinforcing."

— Bill Ackman and Ryan Israel, Pershing Square Q2 Letter

The opportunity to re-enter came as Netflix shares fell roughly 50% from a June 2025 high of $134 to around $67 in mid-June, according to the letter. Ackman argued that concerns about competition from short-form video have proved unfounded and that Netflix's deep pockets can absorb higher compute costs from long-form, high-quality video production.

The fund also highlighted Netflix's ability to convert approximately 90% of its earnings to free cash flow, with its advertising business continuing to scale. Ackman noted that artificial intelligence should "meaningfully enhance the company's content recommendation engine and ad targeting capabilities."

Five Other Bets: Payments, Data, and Eye Care

Beyond Netflix, Pershing Square initiated stakes in Visa and Mastercard, calling them "the highest-quality businesses in the world." The letter described both companies as "capital-light toll-takers" that earn a nominal fee on each transaction without taking material risk, and natural beneficiaries of higher inflation.

Both payment stocks had recently derated to 22 times forward earnings, despite their networks connecting billions of consumers. Ackman dismissed concerns about stablecoin competition, arguing that crypto is growing in markets where cards are not incumbent and that stablecoins cannot offer the fraud protection, credit access, and rewards that credit cards provide.

S&P Global, which Pershing previously owned in 2017, was another pick after AI disruption concerns drove a 25% stock decline in February, pushing its valuation to 19 times earnings from 25 times — what the letter called "a bargain level." Ackman described each of S&P Global's benchmark franchises as "a high-margin, IP licensing business with a formidable competitive moat inside an oligopolistic market structure."

Intercontinental Exchange was flagged for its "highly moated" exchange-operator business that generates nearly 70% of its earnings. Ackman called it "a classic, simple, predictable, free-cash-flow-generative business" that had sold off on unwarranted concerns about cryptocurrency perpetual futures competition.

Rounding out the six new positions was Alcon, the ophthalmology company, which Ackman called "the premier franchise" in its industry, highlighting its global base, surgical vision capabilities, and the anticipated approval of its AURN0001 therapy for corneal edema.

Deploying the New Fund

The investments were made through both Pershing Square Holdings and the newer Pershing Square USA, a $5 billion closed-end fund that began trading on the New York Stock Exchange in late April — the largest closed-end fund IPO in U.S. history.

Ackman and Israel said a stock market "overly focused on artificial-intelligence picks and shovels" had created a "highly attractive environment" for finding undervalued opportunities. The fund has deployed nearly $5 billion in capital since its IPO.

The new positions reflect Ackman's longstanding preference for concentrated, high-conviction bets on companies with durable competitive advantages and strong free cash flow generation — a strategy that has defined his approach across three decades of investing.
